title: System Location Discovery
summary: System location discovery is the collection of clues that indicate where a victim host physically sits. Adversaries use time zone, keyboard layout, and language or locale settings to place a machine in a country or region, and in cloud environments they may read instance metadata to learn the availability zone. On Windows, locale can be read from national language support registry keys or through API functions that return user and system language identifiers, while a Linux or macOS host exposes the same answer through the locale command and the language environment variable. An IP address geolocation lookup performed by the malicious code is another route, although it depends on outbound network access. The result shapes later decisions, including whether the adversary continues, avoids a country, or changes ransomware behaviour. Detection is behavioural, since the underlying reads are ordinary, and useful signals include bursts of locale or registry queries from one process and metadata service requests from workloads that have no reason to make them.

beginner.definition: System location discovery means working out where a computer is. The attacker does not use a map. They read settings such as time zone, keyboard layout, and language. Those settings suggest which country the machine is in.
beginner.whyItMatters: Some attackers skip computers in particular countries to avoid trouble with the police. If your machines do not match their avoid list, they may continue and encrypt your data. Location checks also help them choose which ransom message to show. Spotting these quiet reads gives you a chance to react early.
howItWorks: The attacker runs code on the machine, or uses a tool through a remote session.
They read the time zone and the language settings of the operating system.
They may also read the keyboard layout, which often matches the region.
In the cloud they can ask the instance metadata service for an availability zone.
They may send the public address to an online lookup service for a country.
The answer decides whether they continue the attack, stop quietly, or change their behaviour.
beginner.example: Think of a hotel receptionist who wants to guess where a guest is from without asking. They listen to the language at check in, notice the time shown on the guest's watch, and see which power adapter the guest pulls out of a bag. None of those things proves anything on its own. Together they form a good guess. The guest never filled in a form and nothing was taken from them.
takeaways: Time zone, language, and keyboard layout are used as location clues.
Cloud instance metadata can reveal the region a workload runs in.
These reads are normal on their own, so context is what makes them suspicious.

objectives: List the system settings an adversary uses to infer geographic location.
Explain how cloud instance metadata contributes to location discovery.
Describe how IP address lookup services are used for geolocation.
Explain why location discovery changes follow-on attacker behaviour.
Identify behavioural patterns that make location queries stand out.
